                                           THE VOLUME OF SINGULAR KÄHLER-EINSTEIN FANO VARIETIES

                                                                                      YUCHEN LIU

                                                  Abstract. We show that the anti-canonical volume of an n-dimensional Kähler-Einstein
                                                  Q-Fano variety is bounded from above by certain invariants of the local singularities,
                                                  namely lctn · mult for ideals and the normalized volume function for real valuations.
arXiv:1605.01034v5 [math.AG] 23 May 2018




                                                  This refines a recent result by Fujita. As an application, we get sharp volume upper
                                                  bounds for Kähler-Einstein Fano varieties with quotient singularities. Based on very
                                                  recent results by Li and the author, we show that a Fano manifold is K-semistable if and
                                                  only if a de Fernex-Ein-Mustaţă type inequality holds on its affine cone.



                                                                                  1. Introduction
                                              An n-dimensional complex projective variety X is said to be a Q-Fano variety if X
                                           has klt singularities and −KX is an ample Q-Cartier divisor. When n ≥ 2, the (anti-
                                           canonical) volume ((−KX )n ) of a Q-Fano variety X can be arbitrarily large, such as
                                           volumes of weighted projective spaces (see [Dol82]). In the smooth case, Kollár, Miyaoka,
                                           Mori [KMM92] and Campana [Cam92] showed that there exists a uniform volume upper
                                           bound Cn for n-dimensional Fano manifolds. If n ≤ 3, then Pn has the largest volume
                                           among all n-dimensional Fano manifolds. This fails immediately when n ≥ 4 by examples
                                           of Batyrev [Bat81]. However, if a Q-Fano variety X admits a Kähler-Einstein metric
                                           (in the sense of [BBEGZ11]), then it is expected that Pn has the largest volume (see
                                           [Tia90, OSS16] for n = 2, and [BB11, BB17] for smooth cases). Recently, Fujita [Fuj15]
                                           showed that if X is a n-dimensional Q-Fano variety admitting a Kähler-Einstein metric,
                                           then the anti-canonical volume ((−KX )n ) is less than or equal to (n + 1)n (= the volume
                                           of Pn ).
                                              In this paper, we refine the result [Fuj15] by looking at invariants of the local singular-
                                           ities. Our first main result is the following:
                                           Theorem 1. Let X be a Kähler-Einstein Q-Fano variety. Let p ∈ X be a closed point.
                                           Let Z be a closed subscheme of X with Supp Z = {p}. Then we have
                                                                                    n
                                                                         n         1
                                           (1.1)                  ((−KX ) ) ≤ 1 +       lct(X; IZ )n multZ X,
                                                                                   n
                                           where lct(X; IZ ) is the log canonical threshold of the ideal sheaf IZ , and multZ X is the
                                           Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity of X along Z.
                                             Note that the invariant lctn · mult has been studied by de Fernex, Ein and Mustaţă in
                                           [Mus02, dFEM03, dFEM04, dFM15].
                                             There are three major aspects of Theorem 1:
                                               • If we take Z = p to be a smooth point on X, then lct(X; mp ) = n and multp X = 1.
                                                 In particular, we recover Fujita’s result [Fuj15, Corollary 1.3].
                                             Date: May 24, 2018.

2                                      YUCHEN LIU

                                                   1+ord (K   )
     • By definition, lct(X; IZ ) is the infimum of ordEE (IZY)/X among all prime divisors E
       on a resolution Y of X. Although lct(X; IZ ) is not easy to compute in general, we
       can always get a volume upper bound by considering one divisor E, e.g. Theorem
       3 and 25.
     • On the other hand, if we fix a singularity p on a Kähler-Einstein Q-Fano variety
       X, we get a lower bound of lctn · mult among all thickenings of p. For example,
       if X = Pn then the inequality (1.1) recovers the main result in [dFEM04] (see
       Theorem 22). More generally, we get de Fernex-Ein-Mustaţă type inequalities
       for all cone singularities with K-semistable base using a logarithmic version of
       Theorem 1 (see Theorem 7).
  For a real valuation v on C(X) centered at a closed point p, the normalized volume
          c introduced by C. Li in [Li15], is defined as vol(v)
function vol,                                            c      := AX (v)n · vol(v), where
AX (v) is the log discrepancy of v and vol(v) is the volume of v. The following theorem
gives an upper bound for the anti-canonical volume of X in terms of the normalized
volume of a real valuation.
Theorem 2. Let X be a Kähler-Einstein Q-Fano variety. Let p ∈ X be a closed point.
Let v be a real valuation on C(X) centered at p. Then we have

(1.2)                         ((−KX ) ) ≤ 1 +        vol(v).

   Minimizing the normalized volume function volc has been studied by Li, Xu, Blum and
the author in [Li15, Li17, LL16, LX16, Blu18]. In [LL16], a logarithmic version of Theorem
2 was developed to obtain the sharp lower bound of the normalized volume function for
cone singularities over Kähler-Einstein Q-Fano varieties.
   To compare Theorem 1 and 2, we know from [Mus02, Li15] that the infimum of
                                                                                     c
lct(X; IZ )n · multZ X among all thickenings Z of p is no bigger than the infimum of vol(v)
among all real valuations centered at p. In fact, we show that these two infimums are
the same (see Theorem 27). In particular, this means that Theorem 1 and 2 are actually
equivalent.
  As an application of Theorem 1 and 2, we get sharp volume upper bounds for Kähler-
Einstein Q-Fano varieties with quotient singularities.
Theorem 3. Let X be a Kähler-Einstein Q-Fano variety of dimension n. Let p ∈ X be
a closed point. Suppose (X, p) is a quotient singularity with local analytic model Cn /G
where G ⊂ GL(n, C) acts freely in codimension 1. Then
                                              (n + 1)n
                                  ((−KX )n ) ≤         ,
                                                 |G|
with equality if and only if |G ∩ Gm | = 1 and X ∼= Pn /G, where Gm ⊂ GL(n, C) is the
subgroup consisting of non-zero scalar matrices.
   It is well-known that for algebraic surfaces, klt singularities are the same as quotient
singularities. In [Tia90], Tian showed that the anti-canonical volume of a Kähler-Einstein
log Del Pezzo surface is bounded from above by 48/|G| where G ⊂ GL(2, C) is the orbifold
                        VOLUME OF SINGULAR KE FANO VARIETIES                               3

group at a closed point. In [OSS16], Odaka, Spotti and Sun improved the volume upper
bounds to 12/|G|.
   As a direct consequence of Theorem 3, we get the sharp volume upper bounds 9/|G|
for Kähler-Einstein log Del Pezzo surfaces.
Corollary 4. Let X be a Kähler-Einstein log Del Pezzo surface. Let p ∈ X be a closed
point with local analytic model C2 /G, where G ⊂ GL(2, C) acts freely in codimension 1.
Then

                                                  |G|
with equality if and only if |G ∩ Gm | = 1 and X ∼= P2 /G.
Remark 5. The author was informed by Kento Fujita that he independently obtained
cases of Corollary 4 when (X, p) is Du Val.
  It was conjectured by Cheltsov and Kosta in [CK14, Conjecture 1.18] that a Gorenstein
Del Pezzo surface admits Kähler-Einstein metrics if and only if the singularities are of
certain types depending on the anti-canonical volume. This conjecture was proved by
Odaka, Spotti and Sun in [OSS16, page 165] where Q-Gorenstein smoothable Kähler-
Einstein log Del Pezzo surfaces are classified. As a quick application of Corollary 4, we
give an alternative proof of the “only if” part of this conjecture. We remark that partial
results are known before [OSS16], e.g. [DT92, Jef97, Won13] on the “only if” part and
[MM93, GK07, Che08, Shi10, CK14] on the “if” part.
Corollary 6. Let X be a Kähler-Einstein log Del Pezzo surface with at most Du Val
singularities.
   (1) If ((−KX )2 ) = 1, then X has at most singularities of type A1 , A2 , A3 , A4 , A5 ,
       A6 , A7 or D4 .
   (2) If ((−KX )2 ) = 2, then X has at most singularities of type A1 , A2 or A3 .
   (3) If ((−KX )2 ) = 3, then X has at most singularities of type A1 or A2 .
   (4) If ((−KX )2 ) = 4, then X has at most singularities of type A1 .
   (5) If ((−KX )2 ) ≥ 5, then X is smooth.
  The comparison between Theorem 1 and 2 also allows us to rephrase the results from
[Li17, LL16] in terms of lctn · mult. The following theorem gives a necessary and sufficient
condition for a Fano manifold to be K-semistable.

   The proofs of Theorem 1 and 2 rely on the recent result [Fuj15] where Fujita settled the
optimal volume upper bounds for Ding-semistable Q-Fano varieties. Recall that a Q-Fano
variety X is said to be Ding-semistable if the Ding invariant Ding(X , L) is nonnegative
for any normal test configuration (X , L)/A1 of (X, −rKX ). The results in [Ber16, Section
3] show that, if a Q-Fano variety X admits a Kähler-Einstein metric, then X is Ding-
semistable (see also [Fuj15, Theorem 3.2]). This allows us to prove Theorem 1 and 2 under
the weaker assumption that X is Ding-semistable (see Theorem 16 and 21). To prove the
                                                                            c
equality case of Theorem 3, we blow up a flag ideal associated to the vol-minimizing
valuation to obtain a test configuration with zero CM weight. Then K-polystability
is enough to characterize the Q-Fano variety with maximal volume (see Lemma 33 for
details).
   The paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we recall the notions of Seshadri
constants, Ding-semistability, filtrations and normalized volume of real valuations. As
a generalization of [Fuj15, Theorem 2.3], we characterize the Seshadri constant of an
arbitrary thickening of a close point in terms of the volume function in Lemma 10. In
Section 3.1, we prove Theorem 1 and 2. The proof of Theorem 1 is a quick application of
[Fuj15, Theorem 1.2] and Lemma 10. To prove Theorem 2, we apply [Fuj15, Theorem 4.9]
to the filtration associated to any real valuation. In Section 3.2, we give some applications
of Theorem 1 and 2. We recover the main result from [dFEM04]. We prove the inequality
part of Theorem 3. We also get a volume upper bound for a Ding-semistable Q-Fano
variety with an isolated singularity that is not terminal (see Theorem 25). Section 4
is devoted to comparing the two invariants occurred in the volume upper bounds, i.e.
                  c In Theorem 27, we show that these two invariants have the same
lctn · mult and vol.
infimums among ideals supported (resp. valuations centered) at a klt point. This implies
that Theorem 1 and 2 are equivalent to each other. We prove Theorem 7 using Theorem
27 and results from [Li17, LL16]. In Section 4.2, we study the existence of minimizers
                     c In Section 5, we study the equality case of Theorem 1 and 2.
of lctn · mult and vol.
Lemma 33 characterizes the equality case of Theorem 2 when X is K-polystable with
extra conditions on the real valuation. Applying this lemma, we prove the equality case
of Theorem 3 and Corollary 6. We also prove that Pn is the only Ding-semistable Q-Fano
variety of volume at least (n + 1)n (see Theorem 36). This theorem improves the equality
case of [Fuj15, Theorem 1.1] where Fujita proved for Ding-semistable Fano manifolds.
Notation. Throughout this paper, we work over the complex numbers C. Let X be an
n-dimensional normal variety. Let ∆ be an effective Q-divisor on X such that (X, ∆) is
a klt pair. For a closed subscheme Z of X, the log canonical threshold of its ideal sheaf
IZ with respect to (X, ∆) is defined as
                                        1 + ordE (KY − f ∗ (KX + ∆))
                    lct(X, ∆; IZ ) := inf                            ,
                                      E           ordE (IZ )
where the infimum is taken over all prime divisors E on a log resolution f : Y → (X, ∆).
We also denote by lct(X; IZ ) = lct(X, 0; IZ ) when ∆ = 0. If dim Z = 0, the Hilbert-Samuel
multiplicity of X along Z is defined as
                                                    ℓ(OX /IZk )
                               multZ (X) := lim                 .
                                                k→∞   k n /n!

We will also use the notation lct(a) (and mult(a)) as abbreviation of lct(X; a) (and
multV (a) X) for a coherent ideal sheaf a (of dimension 0) once the variety X is specified.
  Following [BBEGZ11, Ber16], on an n-dimensional Q-Fano variety X, a Kähler metric
ω on the smooth locus Xreg is said to be a Kähler-Einstein
                                                   R           metric on X if it has constant
Ricci curvature, i.e. Ric(ω) = ω on Xreg , and Xreg ω = ((−KX )n ). By [BBEGZ11,
                                                           n

Definition 3.5 and Proposition 3.8], this is equivalent to saying that ω is a closed positive
(1, 1)-current with full Monge-Ampère mass on X satisfying V −1 ω n = µω (see [BBEGZ11,
Section 3] for details).
  Given a normal variety X and a (not necessarily effective) Q-divisor ∆, we say that
(X, ∆) is a sub pair if KX + ∆ is Q-Cartier. Let f : Y → (X, ∆) be a log resolution, then
we have the following equality
                                                     X
                               KY = f ∗ (KX + ∆) +       ai Ei ,
                                                         i

where Ei are distinct prime divisors on Y . We say that (X, ∆) is sub log canonical if
ai ≥ −1 for all i. If D is a Q-Cartier Q-divisor on X, then the log canonical threshold of
D with respect to a sub pair (X, ∆) is defined as
(1.4)        lct(X, ∆; D) := sup{c ∈ R : (X, ∆ + cD) is sub log canonical}.

                                    2. Preliminaries
2.1. Seshadri constants.
Definition 8 ([Laz04]). Let X be a projective variety of dimension n. For a Q-Cartier
Q-divisor L on X, we define the volume of L on X to be
                                                       h0 (X, OX (kL))
                         volX (L) :=      lim sup                      .
                                       k→∞, kL Cartier      k n /n!
We know that the limsup computing volX (L) is actually a limit. If L ≡ L′ , then volX (L) =
volX (L′ ). Moreover, we can extend it uniquely to a continuous function
                                  volX : N 1 (X)R → R≥0 .
Definition 9. Let X be a projective variety, L be an ample Q-Cartier divisor on X.
Let Z be a nonempty proper closed subscheme of X with ideal sheaf IZ . Denote by
σ : X̂ → X the blow up of X along Z. Let F be the Cartier divisor on X̂ given by
OX̂ (−F ) = σ −1 (IZ ) · OX̂ . The Seshadri constant of L along Z, denoted by ǫZ (L), is
defined as
                        ǫZ (L) := sup{x ∈ R>0 | σ ∗ L − xF is ample}.

Lemma 10. Let X be an n-dimensional normal projective variety with n ≥ 2, L be an
ample Q-divisor on X, p ∈ X be a closed point. Let Z be a closed subscheme of X with
Supp Z = {p}. Let σ : X̂ → X be the blow up along Z, and F ⊂ X̂ be the Cartier divisor
defined by the equation OX̂ (−F ) = σ −1 IZ · OX̂ .
    (1) For any x ∈ R≥0 , we have
                  volX̂ (σ ∗ L − xF ) ≥ ((σ ∗ L − xF )n ) = (Ln ) − multZ X · xn .
    (2) Set ΛZ (L) := {x ∈ R≥0 | volX̂ (σ ∗ L − xF ) = ((σ ∗ L − xF )n )}. Then we have
                    ǫZ (L) = max{x ∈ R≥0 | y ∈ ΛZ (L) for all y ∈ [0, x]}.
Proof. The proof goes along the same line as [Fuj15, Theorem 2.3].
   (1) The equality (σ ∗ L − xF )n ) = (Ln ) − multZ X · xn follows from the fact that
multZ (X) = (−1)n−1 (F n ) (see [Ram73]).
   For the inequality part, we can assume that x ∈ Q>0 since the function volX̂ (σ ∗ L − xF )
is continuous. Take any sufficiently large k ∈ Z>0 with kx ∈ Z>0 and kL Cartier. Notice
that we have the long exact sequence
(2.1)     0 → H 0 (X̂, σ ∗ (kL) − kxF ) → H 0 (X̂, σ ∗ (kL)) → H 0 (kxF, σ ∗ (kL)|kxF ) → · · ·
Thus

                                        = h0 (X, kL) − h0 (kxF, OkxF )
Consequently,

Since hi (X̂, σ ∗ (kL) − kxF ) = o(k n ) for i ≥ 2, we conclude that h1 (X̂, σ ∗ (kL) − kxF ) =

   Now let us prove (2). Denote by a the right-hand side of the equation in (2). For any
nef divisor, its volume is equal to its self intersection number. Hence it is obvious that
ǫZ (L) ≤ a. Then it suffices to show that a ≤ ǫZ (L). Equivalently, we only need to show
that for ǫ > 0 sufficiently small with a − ǫ ∈ Q>0 , σ ∗ L − (a − ǫ)F is ample. Fix δ ∈ Q>0
such that δ < ǫZ (L), that is, σ ∗ L − δF is ample. By [dFKL07, Theorem A], we only need
to show that

for any i > 0, any sufficiently small t ∈ Q>0 and suitably divisible m. Denote b :=

Then applying (2.3) yields that hi (X̂, σ ∗ (kL) − kbF ) = o(k n ) for i > 0, sufficiently small
t ∈ Q>0 and suitably divisible k. In other words, (2.4) is true under the same condition
for i, t and m = (1 − t)k. Hence we prove the lemma.                                          

2.2. K-semistability and Ding-semistability. In this section we recall the definition
of K-semistability, and its recent equivalence Ding-semistability.
Definition 11 ([Tia97, Don02], see also [LX14]). Let X be an n-dimensional Q-Fano
variety.
    (a) Let r ∈ Q>0 such that L := −rKX is Cartier. A test configuration (resp. a semi
         test configuration) of (X, L) consists of the following data:
            • a variety X admitting a Gm -action and a Gm -equivariant morphism π : X →
              A1 , where the action of Gm on A1 is given by the standard multiplication;
            • a Gm -equivariant π-ample (resp. π-semiample) line bundle L on X such that
              (X , L)|π−1(A1 \{0}) is equivariantly isomorphic to (X, L) × (A1 \ {0}) with the
              natural Gm -action.
         Moreover, if X is normal in addition, then we say that (X , L)/A1 is a normal test
         configuration (resp. a normal semi test configuration) of (X, L).
   (b) Assume that (X , L) → A1 is a normal test configuration. Let π̄ : (X̄ , L̄) → P1
         be the natural equivariant compactification of (X , L) → A1 . The CM weight
         (equivalently, Donaldson-Futaki invariant) of (X , L) is defined by the intersection
         formula:
                                                                                 
                                      1             n     n+1   n+1 n
            CM(X , L) :=                               (L̄ ) + n (L̄ · KX̄ /P1 ) .
                           (n + 1)((−KX )n ) r n+1               r
    (c)   • The pair (X, −KX ) is called K-semistable if CM(X , L) ≥ 0 for any normal
            test configuration (X , L)/A1 of (X, −rKX ).
          • The pair (X, −KX ) is called K-polystable if CM(X , L) ≥ 0 for any normal
            test configuration (X , L)/A1 of (X, −rKX ), and the equality holds if and only
            if X ∼
                 = X × A1 .
   In [Din88], Ding introduced the so-called Ding functional on the space of Kähler metrics
on Fano manifolds and showed that Kähler-Einstein metrics are critical points of the Ding
functional. Recently, Berman [Ber16] established a formula expressing CM-weights in
terms of the slope of Ding functional along a geodesic ray in the space of all bounded
positively curved metrics on the anti-canonical Q-line bundle of a Q-Fano variety. Later
on, this slope was called Ding invariant by Fujita [Fuj15] in order to define the concept
of Ding-semistability. Next we will recall the recent work by Berman [Ber16] and Fujita
[Fuj15].
Definition 12 ([Ber16, Fuj15]). Let X be an n-dimensional Q-Fano variety.
  (a) Let (X , L)/A1 be a normal semi test configuration of (X, −rKX ) and (X̄ , L̄)/P1
      be its natural compactification. Let D(X ,L) be the Q-divisor on X satisfying the
      following conditions:
         • The support SuppD(X ,L) is contained in X0 .
         • The divisor −rD(X ,L) is a Z-divisor corresponding to the divisorial sheaf
           L̄(rKX̄ /P1 ).
  (b) The Ding invariant Ding(X , L) of (X , L)/A1 is defined as
                                     −(L̄n+1 )                                       
           Ding(X , L) :=                            −  1 −  lct(X , D (X ,L) ; X0 )   .
                             (n + 1)r n+1 ((−KX )n )
      Here lct(X , D(X ,L); X0 ) is defined in the sense of (1.4).
                        VOLUME OF SINGULAR KE FANO VARIETIES                              9

   (c) X is called Ding-semistable if Ding(X , L) ≥ 0 for any normal test configuration
       (X , L)/A1 of (X, −rKX ).
   The following theorem illustrates relations among the existence of Kähler-Einstein met-
rics, K-semistability and Ding-semistability of Q-Fano varieties.
Theorem 13.      (1) If a Q-Fano variety X admits a Kähler-Einstein metric, then X
      is Ding-semistable.
  (2) A Q-Fano variety is K-semistable if and only if it is Ding-semistable.
Proof. (1) is proved by Berman in [Ber16] (see also [Fuj15, Theorem 3.2]).
   (2) The direction that Ding-semistability implies K-semistability is proved by Berman
in [Ber16] using the inequality that Ding(X , L) ≥ CM(X , L) for any normal test con-
figuration (X , L) (see also [Fuj15, Theorem 3.2.2]). The direction that K-semistability
implies Ding-semistability is proved in [BBJ15] based on [LX14] (see also [Fuj16, Section
3]).                                                                                    

2.4. Normalized volume of real valuations. Let (X, p) be a normal Q-Gorenstein
singularity with dim X = n. A real valuation v on the function field C(X) is a map
v : C(X) → R, satisfying:
      • v(f g) = v(f ) + v(g);
      • v(f + g) ≥ min{v(f ), v(g)};
      • v(C∗ ) = 0.
   Denote by Ov := {f ∈ C(X) : v(f ) ≥ 0} the valuation ring of v. Denote by (Op , mp )
the local ring of X at p. We say that a real valuation v on C(X) is centered at p if the local
ring Op is dominated by Ov . In other words, v is nonnegative on Op and strictly positive
on mp . Denote by ValX,p the set of real valuations centered at p. Given a valuation
v ∈ ValX,p , define the valuation ideals for any x ∈ R as follows:
                               ax (v) := {f ∈ OX : v(f ) ≥ x}.
The volume of the valuation v is defined as
                                                       ℓ(OX /ax (v))
                               vol(v) := lim                         .
                                                x→+∞      xn /n!
By [ELS03, Mus02, Cut13], the limit on the right hand side exists and is equal to the
multiplicity of the graded family of ideals a• (v):
                                           mult(am (v))
                        vol(v) = lim                     =: mult(a• (v)).
                                      m→∞       mn
   Following [JM12, BdFFU15], we can define the log discrepancy for any valuation v ∈
ValX . This is achieved in three steps in [JM12, BdFFU15]. Firstly, for a divisorial
valuation ordE associated to a prime divisor E over X, define AX (E) := 1 + ordE (KY /X ),
where π : Y → X is a resolution of X containing E. Next we define the log discrepancy of a
quasi-monomial valuation (also called Abhyankar valuation). For a resolution π : Y → X,
let y := (y1 , · · · , yr ) be a system of algebraic coordinate of a point η ∈ Y . By [JM12,
Proposition 3.1], for every α = (α1 , · · · , αr ) ∈ Rn≥0 one can associate a unique valuation
valα = valy,α ∈ ValX with the following property: whenever f ∈ OY,η is written in O       d Y,η
        P               β                  d
as f =    β∈Z≥0r   cβ y , with each cβ ∈ O  Y,η either zero or a unit, we have

                              valα (f ) = min{hα, βi | cβ 6= 0}.
Such valuations are called quasi-monomial valuations (or equivalently, Abhyankar valua-
                                      P
tions by [ELS03]). Let (Y, D = N        k=1 Dk ) be a log smooth model of X, i.e. π : Y → X

quasi-monomial valuations v that can be described at the point η ∈ Y with respect to
coordinates (y1 , · · · , yr ) such that each yi defines at η an irreducible component of D
(hence η is the generic point of a connected component of the intersection of some of the

                              3. Proofs of main theorems
3.1. Proofs. It was proved by Berman [Ber16] that the existence of a Kähler-Einstein
metric on a Q-Fano variety implies Ding-semistability (see Theorem 13). In this section,
we will prove Theorem 1 and 2 with the weaker assumption that X is Ding-semistable.

3.2. Applications. The following result is an easy consequence of Theorem 1.
Theorem 22 ([dFEM04]). Let X be a variety of dimension n. Let Z be a closed sub-
scheme of X supported at a single smooth closed point. Then
                                          n
                               lct(X; IZ )
                                              multZ X ≥ 1.
                                   n
Proof. It is clear that the multiplicity is preserved under completion. Next, [dFEM11,
Proposition 2.11] implies that lct is also preserved under completion. Hence it suffices to
prove the theorem for X = Pn . This follows directly by applying Theorem 1 to the case
X = Pn .                                                                                 

                                 lct(X; mp ) ≤           ≤ 1.
                                                   bi0
So we finish the proof by applying Theorem 1 to Z = p.                                   

               4. Comparing invariants for ideals and valuations
   In this section, we will always assume that (X, p) is a normal Q-Gorenstein klt singu-
larity of dimension n with p ∈ X a closed point.

Remark 28.      (a) The first equality in (4.1) was observed by Mustaţă in [Mus02] where
      he showed that lct(a• )n · mult(a• ) ≥ nn for any graded sequence of m-primary
      ideals a• of a regular local ring of dimension n. The inequality (4.4) was essentially
      realized by Li in [Li15, Remark 2.8] where he considered the smooth case.
  (b) By Izumi’s theorem, the infimums in Theorem 27 are always positive (see Section
      2.4).
  We will use Theorem 27 to prove Theorem 7 based on [Li17, LL16].

Lemma 32. Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring. Let a• be a graded sequence of m-
primary ideals. Assume that the linear topology on R defined by the filtration a1 ⊃ a2 ⊃ · · ·
is the same as the m-adic topology on R. Assume that ⊕m≥0 am /am+1 is a finitely generated
R/a1 -algebra. Then ⊕m≥0 am is a finitely generated R-algebra.

Proof. We take a set of homogeneous generators of ⊕m≥0 am /am+1 , say x1 , · · · , xr . Let di
be the degree of xi , i.e. xi ∈ adi /adi +1 . Take yi ∈ adi such that xi = yi + adi +1 . Denote by
⊕m≥0 bm the graded R-subalgebra of ⊕m≥0 am generated by y1 , · · · , yr .
  Since {xi } generates ⊕m≥0 am /am+1 , we have am = bm + am+1 . Hence for any l > 0 the
induction yields
                          am = (bm + bm+1 + · · · + bm+l−1 ) + am+l .
Because R is Noetherian, the ideals (bm + bm+1 + · · · + bm+l−1 ) stabilize for l sufficiently
large. Denote the stabilized ideal by cm , then we have am = cm + am+l for l sufficiently
large. Since the filtration a1 ⊃ a2 ⊃ · · · defines the same topology as the m-adic topology,
we may take l sufficiently large such that am+l ⊂ mam . As a result, we have am = cm +mam
which implies that am = cm by Nakayama’s lemma.
   Now it suffices to show that ⊕m≥0 cm is a finitely generated graded R-algebra. By
definition, cm is generated by monomials in {yi } of weighted degree at least m. For
any 0 ≤ j ≤ di , denote by yi,j the homogeneous element yi ∈ aj of degree j. Then
any monomial in {yi } of weighted degree at least m is equal to a monomial in {yi,j } of
weighted degree m. Hence ⊕m≥0 cm is generated by {yi,j } as a graded R-algebra, which
finishes the proof.                                                                         

Lemma 34. Let (X, p) be a normal singularity. Let v∗ be a divisorial valuation on
X centered at p. Assume that grv∗ OX,p is a finitely generated C-algebra. Let F :=
Proj grv∗ OX,p . Define X̂ := ProjX ⊕m≥0 am (v∗ ) with the projection σ : X̂ → X. Then
X̂ is normal, F = Ex(σ) is a Q-Cartier prime divisor on X̂, and v∗ = ordF . (Note that
σ is called a prime blow-up in [Ish04].)
Proof. By Lemma 32, we know that ⊕m≥0 am (v∗ ) is a finitely generated OX -algebra. Since
the valuation ideals am (v∗ ) are always integrally closed, X̂ is normal. By definition of F
we know that the ideal sheaf IF is the same as the coherent sheaf OX̂ (1). Let k ∈ Z>0
be sufficiently divisible so that amk (v∗ ) = ak (v∗ )m for any positive integer m. Thus X̂
is naturally isomorphic to the blow up of X along the ideal sheaf ak (v∗ ). In particular,
OX̂ (k) = σ −1 ak (v∗ ) · OX̂ is an invertible ideal sheaf. Next, OX̂ /OX̂ (k) is supported at the
exceptional locus of σ. As ideal sheaves on X̂, we know that OX̂ (1)k ⊂ OX̂ (k) ⊂ OX̂ (1).
Hence OX̂ (1) and OX̂ (k) have the same nilradical as ideal sheaves, and
                       Fred = Supp(OX̂ /OX̂ (1)) = Supp(OX̂ /OX̂ (k))
which is the reduced exceptional locus of σ. On the other hand, it is easy to see that
grv∗ OX,p is an integral domain, so F is an integral scheme.
   For k sufficiently divisible, we have that OX̂ (k) is invertible and σ∗ OX̂ (mk) = amk (v∗ )
for any m ∈ Z≥0 . Thus OX̂ (k) = OX̂ (−lF ) for some positive integer l (so F is Q-Cartier).
24                                     YUCHEN LIU

Then for any m ∈ Z≥0 we have the following equivalences:
               v∗ (f ) ≥ m ⇔ v∗ (f k ) ≥ mk ⇔ f k ∈ amk (v∗ ) ⇔ σ ∗ f k ∈ OX̂ (mk)
                                                                ml
                           ⇔ ordF (σ ∗ f k ) ≥ ml ⇔ ordF (f ) ≥    .
                                                                k
Assume v∗ (f ) = m. If ordF (f ) > ml/k, then we have ordF (f ) ≥ (ml + 1)/k. Hence
ordF (f l ) ≥ (ml + 1)l/k which implies that v∗ (f l ) ≥ ml + 1, a contradiction! Hence we
have ordF = (l/k)v∗ . Therefore, v∗ = ordF since both v∗ and ordF are divisorial.        
Lemma 35. Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring. Let p, q be two prime ideals in R
satisfying that p + q = m, p ∩ q = pq and R/q is a DVR. Then p is principal.
Proof. Let x + q be a uniformizer of R/q. Since m = p + q, we may choose x so that x ∈ p.
Hence we have (x) + q = m. As a result,
                               p = (x) + p ∩ q = (x) + pq.
So p = (x) by Nakayama lemma.                                                           
5.2. Applications. The following theorem improves Fujita’s result on the equality case
in [Fuj15, Theorem 5.1].
Theorem 36. Let X be a Ding-semistable Q-Fano variety of dimension n. If ((−KX )n ) ≥
(n + 1)n , then X ∼
                  = Pn .
Proof 1. Notice that ((−KX )n ) ≤ (n + 1)n by [Fuj15, Corollary 1.3]. Thus we have
((−KX )n ) = (n + 1)n . Let p ∈ X be a smooth point. From [Fuj15, Proof of Theorem
5.1] or Remark 17, we see that ǫp (−KX ) = n + 1. Then the theorem is a consequence
of the forthcoming paper [LZ16] (joint with Ziquan Zhuang), where we show that if an
n-dimensional Q-Fano variety X satisfies ǫp (−KX ) > n for some smooth point p ∈ X,
then X ∼= Pn .                                                                     
Proof 2. We follow the strategy and notation of the proof of Lemma 33. Let v∗ := ordp
for a smooth point p ∈ X. As argued in the first proof, the assumptions of Lemma 33 are
fulfilled except that X is only Ding-semistable rather than K-polystable. Nevertheless,
we still have a semi Q-test configuration (X , L) of (X, −KX ) such that L⊥ = X̂ and
CM(X , L) = 0. Let (Y, M) be the ample model of (X , L)/A1, with h : X → Y and
L = h∗ M. We will show that Y0 ∼ = Pn .
   Following the proof of Lemma 33, we know that h|E : E → Y0 is a finite birational
morphism. Since v∗ = ordp and p ∈ X is a smooth point, we have that E ∼ = Pn . Therefore,
E is the normalization of Y0 . Consider the short exact sequence
                            0 → OX (−E) → OX → OE → 0.
By taking h∗ , we get a long exact sequence
(5.1)           0 → h∗ OX (−E) → OY → h∗ OE → R1 h∗ OX (−E) → · · ·
Since X0 = X̂ + E, we have that h∗ OX (−E) = OY (−Y0 ) ⊗ h∗ OX (X̂). Notice that X̂ is
h-exceptional, hence h∗ OX (X̂) = OY . As a result, h∗ OX (−E) ∼
                                                               = OY (−Y0 ). On the other
hand, we have
                h∗ M = L = g ∗ (−KX×A1 /A1 ) − (n + 1)E = −KX /A1 − E.
                         VOLUME OF SINGULAR KE FANO VARIETIES                                  25

So −E = KX /A1 +h∗ M ∼Q,h KX . Since X has klt singularities, we have that R1 h∗ OX (−E) =
0 by the generalized Kodaira vanishing theorem [Kol95, Theorem 10.19.4]. Thus the exact
sequence (5.1) yields that h∗ OE = OY0 , which implies Y0 ∼
                                                          =E∼ = Pn .
          n
  Since P is rigid under smooth deformation (cf. [Kol96, Exercise V.1.11.12.2]), we
conclude that Yt ∼                                       = Xt ∼
                  = Pn for general t ∈ A1 \ {0}, hence X ∼    = Yt ∼
                                                                   = Pn .              
  In the following theorem, we show the equality case of Theorem 3.
Theorem 37. Let X be a Kähler-Einstein Q-Fano variety. Let p ∈ X be a closed
point. Suppose (X, p) is a quotient singularity with local analytic model Cn /G, where
G ⊂ GL(n, C) acts freely in codimension 1. Then ((−KX )n ) = (n + 1)n /|G| if and only
if |G ∩ Gm | = 1 and X ∼
                       = Pn /G.
Proof. For the “if” part, we may assume that G ⊂ U(n). Hence G preserves the Fubini-
Study metric ωF S on Pn . Since |G ∩ Gm | = 1, the G-action on Pn is free in codimen-
sion 1. This implies that the quotient metric of ωF S on Pn /G is Kähler-Einstein and
((−KPn /G )n ) = ((−KPn )n )/|G| = (n + 1)n /|G|.
   For the “only if” part, let (Y, o) := (Cn /G, 0) be the local analytic model of (X, p). Let
d := |G ∩Gm |. Following the proof of Theorem 23, we have a partial resolution h : Ŷ → Y
of Y that is the quotient of the blow up g : C cn → Cn . Since Ŷ is the quotient of C cn , it has
                                                                               ∼    n−1
klt singularities. Denote by F the exceptional divisor of h, then we have F = P /G. Let
u∗ := ordF be the divisorial on Y centered at o, then we have gru∗ OY,o ∼   = C[x1 , · · · , xn ]G
is a finitely generated C-algebra. (Here we assume deg xi = 1/d so that the grading is

By [Ber16] we have that X is K-polystable. Hence applying Lemma 33 yields

Remark 38.      (1) The restriction on G in Theorem 37 can be dropped in its logarithmic
      version as follows: suppose (X, D) is a conical Kähler-Einstein log Fano pair,
      p 6∈ Supp(D), (X, p) is analytically isomorphic to (Cn /G, 0) and ((−KX − D)n ) =
      (n + 1)n /|G|, then (X, D) ∼= (Pn /G, (1 − d1 )H∞ /G) where d = |G ∩ Gm |.
  (2) The K-polystable condtion in Lemma 33 and Kähler-Einstein condition in Theo-
      rem 3 cannot be dropped since any cubic surface in P3 with only one or two A2
      singularities is K-semistable but not K-polystable (hence not Kähler-Einstein) ac-
      cording to [OSS16, Section 4.2], but all global quotients of P2 are Kähler-Einstein
      (hence K-polystable).
Corollary 39 (=Corollary 6). Let X be a Kähler-Einstein log Del Pezzo surface with at
most Du Val singularities.
     (1) If ((−KX )2 ) = 1, then X has at most singularities of type A1 , A2 , A3 , A4 , A5 ,
         A6 , A7 or D4 .
     (2) If ((−KX )2 ) = 2, then X has at most singularities of type A1 , A2 or A3 .
     (3) If ((−KX )2 ) = 3, then X has at most singularities of type A1 or A2 .
     (4) If ((−KX )2 ) = 4, then X has at most singularities of type A1 .
     (5) If ((−KX )2 ) ≥ 5, then X is smooth.
Proof. Let C2 /G be the local analytic model of (X, p) for any closed point p ∈ X. By
Corollary 4, we know that |G| ≤ 9/((−KX )2 ).
   Recall that the order of orbifold group at an Ak singularity is k + 1, a Dk singularity
is 4(k − 2), an E6 singularity is 24, an E7 singularity is 48, and an E8 singularity is
120. Hence the inequality |G| ≤ 9/((−KX )2 ) implies (2)(3)(4)(5). For part (1), the same
argument yields that X has at most singularities type of Ak with k ≤ 8, or of type D4 .
Hence we only need to rule out A8 cases.
   Assume to the contrary that (X, p) is of type A8 . Since ((−KX )2 ) = 1 = 9/|G|,
Theorem 37 implies that X ∼  = P2 /G, where G = Z/9Z acts on P2 as follows:
                             [x, y, z] 7→ [ζ i x, ζ −i y, z] for i ∈ Z/9Z,
               2πi
where ζ := e 9 is the ninth root of unity. The point p is the quotient of [0, 0, 1] under
this action, which is of type 19 (1, −1) as a cyclic quotient singularity. However, the quo-
tient singularities at [1, 0, 0] and [0, 1, 0] are both of type 91 (1, 2) which are not Du Val,
contradiction!                                                                               
